title: Average Days Between Customer Orders
description:
For each customer, compute the **average number of days between consecutive orders**. Only include customers with 2 or more orders.

**Table: orders** — `id`, `customer_id`, `order_date`, `status`, `total_amount`

Output columns: `customer_id`, `avg_days_between_orders`. Round to 1 decimal. Order by `customer_id`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer_id INT, order_date DATE, status VARCHAR, total_amount DECIMAL); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1,DATE '2026-01-05','completed',100.00),(2,1,DATE '2026-01-20','completed',200.00),(3,1,DATE '2026-02-10','completed',150.00),(4,2,DATE '2026-01-10','completed',300.00),(5,2,DATE '2026-03-10','completed',250.00),(6,3,DATE '2026-01-15','completed',80.00);
solution_sql: WITH gaps AS (SELECT customer_id, order_date, DATE_DIFF('day', LAG(order_date) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date), order_date) AS days_since_prev FROM orders) SELECT customer_id, ROUND(AVG(days_since_prev), 1) AS avg_days_between_orders FROM gaps WHERE days_since_prev IS NOT NULL GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY customer_id

test_cases.description: Customer 1 avg ~18.5 days; customer 2 avg 59 days; customer 3 excluded (1 order)

hints: LAG(order_date) OVER (PARTITION BY customer ORDER BY order_date) gives the previous order date.
DATE_DIFF('day', prev_date, curr_date) computes the gap in days.
explanation: LAG gives the previous order date per customer. DATE_DIFF computes the gap. The CTE builds a 'days_since_prev' column; the outer query averages it. Customer 3 has only one order so no LAG value exists — they're excluded via IS NOT NULL.
